chunks: And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Abu Ubayda al-Hadhdha', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever teaches a subject of guidance, for him is the like of the reward of whoever acts upon it, and nothing will be reduced from their rewards; and whoever teaches a subject of misguidance, upon him shall be the like of the burdens of whoever acts upon it, and nothing will be reduced from their burdens.

key_terms.أَجْر: Recompense/reward — the divine reward for righteous action
key_terms.أَوْزَار: Burdens/sins — the weight of wrongdoing borne in the afterlife
key_terms.بَابُ ضَلَالٍ: A subject/chapter of misguidance — teaching that leads people away from the truth
key_terms.بَابُ هُدًى: A subject/chapter of guidance — in classical usage, 'bab' (door/chapter) was used to denote a field or topic of knowledge

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for a teacher of Islamic knowledge according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes a foundational principle of moral accountability in teaching: a teacher of guidance shares equally in the reward of every student who acts upon that guidance, without diminishing the students' own rewards. Conversely, a teacher of misguidance bears a proportional burden equal to the sins of all who follow that misguidance. This teaching would have been understood by the original audience in the context of the early Islamic scholarly tradition, where transmitting knowledge carried immense responsibility — both as a vehicle of divine guidance and as a potential source of corruption.

en.hubeali:
And by this chain, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Hameed, from Al A’ala Bin Razen, from Abu Ubeyda Al Haza’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who teaches a door (subject) of guidance, for him would be a Recompense similar to the one who acts by it and there would not be any reduction from Recompense (of those who act upon it); and the one who teaches a door (subject) of straying, there would be upon him a burden similar to the one who acts by it, and there would not be any reduction in their burdens - by anything’.
en.sarwar: 4. Through the same chain of narrator it is narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from abu ‘Ubayda al-Hadhdha’ from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following. “

Whoever teaches a subject of guidance he will receive a reward equal to the rewards of those who would practice such guidance without any reduction in the rewards of the later ones. Whoever would introduce a subject of misguidance he will suffer equal to the suffering due for each time it is practiced without any reduction in the suffering of whoever would practice such misguidance.”
